places.name: Fort De Soto Park
places.hours_text: Daily, 7 a.m. to sunset; open all year. Gulf and Bay piers 7 a.m. to sunset.
places.price_text: $6 daily parking fee (pay stations, mobile app or pay-by-text). Concessions and rentals are cashless.
places.summary: Pinellas County's largest park: 1,136 acres on five connected keys with almost three miles of beach (including the only county-park beach where dogs are allowed, in a designated area), two fishing piers, a 236-site campground, seven miles of paved trail, kayak and canoe trails, and the fort's historic mortar battery. Ferries leave from the park for Egmont Key and Shell Key.
places.quote: The largest park within the Pinellas County Park System, Fort De Soto park consists of 1,136 acres made up of five interconnected islands (keys).

heritage.story: Pinellas County bought the land from the federal government in 1938, sold it back in 1941 for use as a gunnery and bombing range during World War II, and repurchased it in 1948. The 12-inch mortar battery at the fort the park is named for was listed in the National Register of Historic Places in 1977. Two British rapid-fire rifles of 1890 vintage were installed in 1982, and markers show where the original buildings stood.
heritage.visiting: The battery, the historic-fort guide and the Quartermaster Storehouse Museum are inside the park, open 7 a.m. to sunset.

places.status_note: Open. The far end of the Bay Pier is closed for hurricane repairs; boat-ramp floating docks are being replaced in phases through the winter; main road and trail repaving runs from September 2026 to early 2027; the park is closed until 9 a.m. on Oct. 18, Oct. 31 and Nov. 14, 2026 for races (county park updates page, updated Sep 25, 2026).
places.accessibility: A 2,200-foot Barrier-Free Nature Trail is a self-guided interpretive trail open to visitors of all physical abilities.
places.parking_text: $6 per day. Pinellas County's park updates page (updated Sep 25, 2026) says county beach parking becomes $3.50 per hour, capped at $12 per day, plus tax, from Dec. 1, 2026.
places.notes: Shared id (see README). Attendance 'more than 2.7 million visitors' and the Dr. Beach / Tripadvisor awards are on the county page. Park coordinates are the OSM park polygon centroid (Photon).

places.name: Sand Key Park
places.hours_text: Daily, 7 a.m. to sunset; closed the day after Thanksgiving and Dec. 25.
places.price_text: $6 daily beach parking (credit cards only at pay stations).
places.summary: A 95-acre county beach park on Sand Key in Clearwater, with a Gulf beach with seasonal lifeguards, a boardwalk nature trail by a salt marsh, bathhouses, a dog park, a playground and umbrella and cabana rentals.
places.quote: This park has a white sandy beach with seasonal lifeguards and sea turtles that nest from April – October.
places.status_note: Open. A repaired seawall section stays closed until October 2026 as equipment staging for the City of Clearwater's marina construction (county park updates page, updated Sep 25, 2026).
places.parking_text: $6 per day at pay-by-plate stations (Visa, Mastercard, American Express). Pinellas County's park updates page (updated Sep 25, 2026) says county beach parking becomes $3.50 per hour, capped at $12 per day, plus tax, from Dec. 1, 2026.
places.notes: The park page itself still says the seawall section closes 'until August 2026'; the Sep 25 updates page says October 2026.

places.name: Fred Howard Park
places.hours_text: Daily, 7 a.m. to sunset; closed the day after Thanksgiving and Dec. 25.
places.price_text: $6 daily beach parking.
places.summary: A 155-acre county park in Tarpon Springs where a 1-mile causeway leads to a Gulf beach used for swimming, windsurfing, kayak launching and sunsets; the mainland side has picnic shelters, playgrounds and a ball field.
places.quote: There is a 1-mile causeway from the park to the white sandy beach for swimming and sunsets.
places.parking_text: $6 per day at pay-by-plate stations or by mobile app. Pinellas County's park updates page (updated Sep 25, 2026) says county beach parking becomes $3.50 per hour, capped at $12 per day, plus tax, from Dec. 1, 2026.
places.notes: Named for Fred H. Howard, Tarpon Springs mayor first elected in 1945 (county page).

places.name: John Chesnut Sr. Park
places.hours_text: Daily, 7 a.m. to sunset; closed the day after Thanksgiving and Dec. 25.
places.price_text: Boat ramp fee charged.
places.summary: A 255-acre county park on Lake Tarpon with nature trails, a canoe trail for non-motorized boats, a boat ramp, a dog park, two playgrounds and 13 picnic shelters. Swimming is not allowed.
places.status_note: Open. Ten picnic shelters are out of service, and an 8.5-acre pond is being treated for exotic plants in sections over 12 months from May 2026 (county park updates page, updated Sep 25, 2026).

places.name: Lake Seminole Park
places.hours_text: Daily, 7 a.m. to sunset; closed the day after Thanksgiving and Dec. 25.
places.summary: A 258-acre county park and wildlife sanctuary on Lake Seminole with a three-mile paved loop for walking, skating and cycling, boat ramps, lake fishing, playgrounds and 13 picnic shelters. Swimming is not permitted.
places.quote: Lake Seminole Park is 258 acres of designated wildlife habitat and sanctuary located in Seminole.
places.accessibility: The county lists the park as wheelchair accessible.

places.name: Philippe Park
places.hours_text: Daily, 7 a.m. to sunset; closed the day after Thanksgiving and Dec. 25.
places.price_text: Boat ramp fee charged.
places.summary: Pinellas County's oldest park, 92 acres in Safety Harbor, shaded by large trees and home to the Tocobaga temple mound; it also has picnic shelters, a boat ramp, fishing and playgrounds.
places.quote: The Temple Mound was built by Native Americans known as the Tocobaga. It is the largest remaining mound in the Tampa Bay region

designations.name: National Register of Historic Places (Safety Harbor Site)

heritage.story: The park holds the Safety Harbor Site, identified as Tocobaga, capital of the Tocobaga people in the 16th century, and the type site of the Safety Harbor culture. Its temple mound, built of alternating layers of shell and sand, is about 150 feet across and 20 feet high; the county says it is the largest remaining mound in the Tampa Bay region. Pinellas County acquired the property in 1948, and the site was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1964.
heritage.visiting: The mound is inside the park, open daily 7 a.m. to sunset.

places.status_note: Open. The main playground is closed while a new one is built (work expected fall to winter 2026), and restrooms 1, 5 and 8 are closed for plumbing repairs (county park updates page, updated Sep 25, 2026).
places.notes: The county page calls the mound 'listed in the National Register of Historic Landmarks'; the NHL (1964) and NRHP (66000270, 1966) details are from Wikipedia's Safety Harbor Site article. history-region may hold a separate safety-harbor-site record; the merge should link them.

places.name: Sawgrass Lake Park
places.hours_text: Daily, 7 a.m. to sunset; closed the day after Thanksgiving and Dec. 25.
places.summary: A 400-acre park in the Lealman community run with the Southwest Florida Water Management District, with a boardwalk and nature trail through a maple swamp and an observation tower; thousands of birds pass through in fall and spring. Fishing is not allowed.
places.quote: This park has one of the largest maple swamps on the Gulf Coast, which allows people to view a variety of wildlife.

places.name: Brooker Creek Preserve
places.hours_text: Preserve and hiking trails: daily, 7 a.m. to about one hour before sunset. Environmental Education Center: Thursday to Saturday 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., Sunday 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. Closed the day after Thanksgiving and Dec. 25.
places.summary: An 8,700-acre conservation area in northeastern Pinellas County that protects part of the drinking-water supply; visitors use its hiking trails, guided tours and the Environmental Education Center's exhibits.
places.quote: At about 8,700 acres, Brooker Creek Preserve is a significant conservation area in the northeastern corner of Pinellas County
places.notes: Area set to palm-harbor (East Lake side of north county); the mailing city is Tarpon Springs.

places.name: Shell Key Preserve
places.hours_text: Open 24 hours a day, including holidays.
places.price_text: Camping permit $6 per day, up to six people (does not include Fort De Soto boat-ramp parking).
places.summary: An 1,800-acre county preserve of undeveloped barrier island, mangrove islands and seagrass beds, reached only by boat or the ferry from Fort De Soto's boat ramp. Beach use and permit camping are allowed at the island's north and south ends; the middle is closed to protect nesting shorebirds, and there are no restrooms.
places.quote: Shell Key is one of the state’s most important areas for shorebird nesting and wintering and serves as an important study area for these species.
places.notes: County lists 2187 Oceanview Drive, Tierra Verde as the preserve address; omitted from address because the island is reached only by boat. Coordinates from Wikipedia (Shell Key Preserve); Photon's 'Shell Key' is a different island in Hillsborough County.

places.name: Weedon Island Preserve
places.hours_text: Preserve and trails: daily, 7 a.m. to about 15 minutes before sunset. Cultural and Natural History Center: Thursday to Saturday 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., Sunday 11 a.m. to 4 p.m.
places.summary: A 3,000-acre preserve on Tampa Bay in north St. Petersburg with more than 4.7 miles of boardwalks and trails, a fishing pier, paddling trails and the Cultural and Natural History Center; Indigenous peoples lived here for thousands of years.
places.quote: Indigenous peoples, including those during the “Weeden” (alternate spelling) Island Cultural Period, lived at this site for thousands of years.
places.status_note: Open. Part of the Bay Boardwalk is closed for repairs until late 2026, the north paddling trail is closed, and the preserve is closed until noon on Oct. 24, 2026 for a trail run (county park and park-updates pages).

places.name: Florida Botanical Gardens
places.hours_text: Daily, 7 a.m. to 5 p.m.; closed the day after Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.
places.price_text: Free admission.
places.summary: A free 150-acre county garden in Largo with formal gardens, landscapes and native habitats; leashed pets are welcome. Entrances are on Ulmerton Road and Walsingham Road.
places.quote: Visitors to the Florida Botanical Gardens can relish the natural wonder of Florida while enjoying a walk through 150 acres of formal gardens, scenic landscapes, and native habitats.
places.notes: Hours conflict: the garden page says 7 a.m. to 5 p.m.; the county park-hours page says 7 a.m. to sunset. Used the garden page. Second entrance: 12211 Walsingham Road.

places.name: Wall Springs Park
places.hours_text: Daily, 7 a.m. to sunset; closed the day after Thanksgiving and Dec. 25.
places.summary: A 210-acre county park on the Pinellas Trail in Palm Harbor with a boardwalk and viewing area at a natural spring once used as a spa and bathing area, and a 35-foot observation tower with Gulf views.
places.quote: This park provides a viewing area and boardwalk of the natural spring that once was used as a spa and bathing area.
places.status_note: Open. The playground is closed from Sep. 28, 2026 while a new one is installed, expected by winter 2026 (county park updates page).
places.notes: Coastal Addition entrance: 621 Wai Lani Road, Palm Harbor.

places.name: Boca Ciega Millennium Park
places.hours_text: Daily, 7 a.m. to sunset; closed the day after Thanksgiving and Dec. 25.
places.summary: A 186-acre county park in Seminole on Boca Ciega Bay with a 35-foot observation tower, boardwalks, a nature trail, a dog park and a Pinellas Trail connection; it is on the Great Florida Birding Trail.
places.quote: In 2007, a major discovery of Pleistocene age fossils offered a much older history of Boca Ciega Millennium Park.

places.name: Indian Rocks Beach Access
places.price_text: Parking fee charged.
places.summary: A county beach access in Indian Rocks Beach with paid parking, restrooms and showers.
places.notes: Census matched the address in ZIP 33785; the county page gives 34635.

places.name: Tiki Gardens / Indian Shores Beach Access
places.price_text: Paid parking, enforced by the Town of Indian Shores.
places.summary: A 9.9-acre county beach access in Indian Shores with a 170-space paid lot, restrooms, beach showers and a pedestrian crossing light on Gulf Boulevard.

places.name: Redington Shores Beach Access
places.price_text: Parking fee charged.
places.summary: A 3.5-acre county beach access in Redington Shores with a 400-foot-wide beach, 170 paid parking spaces, restrooms and beach showers.

places.name: Madeira Beach Access
places.price_text: Paid parking for 104 vehicles (credit cards only at pay stations).
places.summary: A 1.5-acre county beach access with 450 feet of Gulf beach in Madeira Beach, restrooms, beach showers and 104 paid parking spaces.

places.name: St. Pete Beach Access
places.price_text: Parking fee charged.
places.summary: A county beach access in St. Pete Beach with 235 paid parking spaces, three boardwalks to the sand, restrooms, showers and a water fountain.

places.name: Lettuce Lake Conservation Park
places.hours_text: Spring and summer 8 a.m. to 7 p.m.; fall and winter 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.
places.price_text: $2 per vehicle (cash only), up to 8 people.
places.summary: A Hillsborough County park on the Hillsborough River floodplain, much of it hardwood swamp, with a 3,500-foot boardwalk, a 1.25-mile paved trail, a visitors center, a native plant garden and new playgrounds. Pets and bicycles are not allowed on the boardwalk.
places.quote: Lettuce Lake Conservation Park is one of Hillsborough County's most popular parks.
places.status_note: Open, with repairs: sections of the boardwalk, shelters 5 and 7, the observation tower and the canoe and kayak launch are closed, and canoe and kayak rentals are suspended (county notice updated Aug 13, 2026).

places.name: E.G. Simmons Conservation Park
places.hours_text: Spring and summer 8 a.m. to 7 p.m.; fall and winter 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.
places.price_text: $2 per vehicle, up to 8 people; $5 boat launch; camping and rentals extra.
places.summary: A Hillsborough County park on Tampa Bay north of Ruskin with 700 feet of bay beach and a swimming area, a 200-acre mangrove bird sanctuary, a fishing pier, kayak rentals, a boat ramp and a 110-site campground.
places.quote: Developed from 258 acres of native mangroves with open land areas and intertwined with waterways, the park also includes 200 acres of mangrove swamp that has been especially reserved for a bird and wildlife sanctuary

places.name: Apollo Beach Nature Preserve
places.hours_text: Sunrise to sunset; closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.
places.summary: A 63-acre Hillsborough County preserve on Tampa Bay with a 2-acre sandy beach for picnicking and sunbathing (no swimming), a 37-foot wheelchair-accessible observation tower and shoreline fishing. Pets are allowed but not on the tower.
places.quote: Seven acres of the preserve are separated from the habitat restoration areas and dedicated to nature-based recreation, which includes a 2-acre sandy beach for picnicking and sunbathing (no swimming allowed)
places.accessibility: The 37-foot observation tower is wheelchair accessible.
places.notes: Hours: the preserve page lists none; the county holiday page says non-staffed nature preserves are open sunrise to sunset year round, and lists Apollo Beach Nature Preserve as closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.

places.name: Upper Tampa Bay Conservation Park
places.hours_text: Daily, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.
places.price_text: $2 per vehicle, up to 8 people; rentals extra.
places.summary: A 596-acre Hillsborough County peninsula park founded in 1982, with nature trails and boardwalks through mangroves, marshes and pine flatwoods, a canoe and kayak launch with rentals, and a nature center with live animal displays.
places.quote: Hillsborough County founded the Upper Tampa Bay Conservation Park in 1982 to provide a protected area for nature study and passive recreation.
places.notes: Park phone listed as (813) 855-1765 at the top and (813) 844-1765 in the paddling section.

places.name: Lithia Springs Conservation Park
places.hours_text: Spring and summer 8 a.m. to 7 p.m.; fall and winter 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. The swimming area closes 1 hour before the park; swim sessions 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. and 2 p.m. to 6 p.m., 200 swimmers each.
places.price_text: $2 per vehicle, up to 8 people; swimming $2 per person.
places.summary: A 160-acre Hillsborough County park built around a natural spring that flows into the Alafia River; the spring stays about 72 degrees, so people swim year round. It also has woodland trails, a playground and a 45-site campground. Pets are not allowed in the spring area.
places.quote: But it is the natural spring that serves as the park’s major attraction, which---courtesy of the water’s 72 degree temperature---provides an excellent swimming experience all year long.
places.status_note: Open. The county says the swimming area reaches maximum capacity on weekends; swim bands are sold only at the park, for one of two daily sessions.

places.name: Edward Medard Conservation Park
places.hours_text: Spring and summer 8 a.m. to 7 p.m.; fall and winter 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.
places.price_text: $2 per vehicle, up to 8 people; $5 boat launch; camping and rentals extra.
places.summary: A Hillsborough County regional park around a 700-acre reservoir used for canoeing, boating and fishing, with a 3-mile trail for hikers and riders who bring their own horses, disc golf, a boardwalk, an observation platform and a 43-site campground.
places.status_note: Open. The boat ramp is closed while the Southwest Florida Water Management District partially draws down the Medard Reservoir; canoes and kayaks should not be affected (county page).

places.name: Alderman's Ford Conservation Park
places.hours_text: Spring and summer 8 a.m. to 7 p.m.; fall and winter 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. The canoe-launch entrance opens at 7 a.m.
places.price_text: $2 per vehicle, up to 8 people; rentals extra.
places.summary: A Hillsborough County park at the 1848 river crossing of settler James Alderman, with a 1.9-mile paved loop along the north and south prongs of the Alafia River, a boardwalk, a canoe launch and four hike-in primitive campsites. Swimming is not permitted.
places.quote: The park's most popular attraction is a 1.9 mile paved loop that follows the north and south prongs of the Alafia River-- one of the most popular canoe spots in the state.
places.notes: Canoe launch entrance: 9625 Canoe Launch Loop, Lithia, FL 33547.

places.name: Flatwoods Conservation Park
places.hours_text: Fall and winter 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.; spring and summer 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.
places.price_text: $2 per vehicle, up to 8 people.
places.summary: A Hillsborough County park known for its seven-mile paved loop road used as a multiuse trail, with off-road bike trails and nature trails; a two-mile paved extension connects to Bruce B. Downs Boulevard in New Tampa.
places.notes: Second entrance: 18205 Bruce B. Downs Blvd. Coordinates are Photon's 'Flatwoods Park Trail' road, inside the park; area set to north-tampa (New Tampa side).

places.name: Eureka Springs Conservation Park
places.hours_text: Daily, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.
places.price_text: $2 per vehicle, up to 8 people.
places.summary: A 31-acre botanical garden that botanist Albert Greenburg began in 1938 and gave to Hillsborough County in 1967, with a fern collection, a rose garden, an orchid room, a greenhouse and boardwalks through a floodplain forest.
places.quote: Lovers of horticulture will savor the 31-acre natural beauty, especially the largest publicly owned collection of ferns in Florida.
places.status_note: Open. The roses near the pergola are pruned from Jan. 6, 2027, with few blooms until about April 2027 (county page).

places.name: Upper Tampa Bay Trail
places.hours_text: Sunrise to sunset.
places.price_text: $2 per vehicle at trailhead parking, up to 8 people.
places.summary: A paved Hillsborough County trail in the northwest of the county, from a trailhead near Memorial Highway north along Channel A to Peterson Road Park, then on to Lutz Lake Fern Road, where it connects to the Suncoast Trail; it has six trailheads.
places.notes: Point is the Channel Park Trailhead (main entrance), 9201 W. Waters Ave.

places.name: Ben T. Davis Beach
places.hours_text: Sunrise to sunset.
places.price_text: Metered parking, $2.50 per hour.
places.summary: A City of Tampa bay beach on the Courtney Campbell Causeway; the state health department tests its water under the Florida Healthy Beaches Program.
places.notes: Tampa's advisories page (Sep 24, 2026): no advisories at any city beach. Point is Photon's OSM feature for the beach; census point for the address is 300 m east.

places.name: Picnic Island Park
places.hours_text: Sunrise to sunset; boat ramp open 24 hours.
places.summary: A City of Tampa park in far South Tampa with a bay beach, a separate gated dog beach south of the fishing pier, a boat ramp, a disc golf course, a sand volleyball court and a playground; a mangrove-tunnel kayak launch is across the street.
places.quote: There is also a separate, gated dog beach just south of the fishing pier.

places.name: Cypress Point Park
places.hours_text: Sunrise to sunset.
places.price_text: Free parking weekdays until noon; otherwise metered, $1 the first hour and $2 each hour after.
places.summary: A City of Tampa park on Tampa Bay with a bay beach, paved and unpaved shaded trails, a disc golf course, a sand volleyball court and a self-service paddleboard rental station; planes landing at Tampa International pass overhead.
places.quote: The calm and tranquil white sand beach of Cypress Point offers breathtaking views of Tampa Bay with occasional flyovers from planes landing at Tampa International Airport.

places.name: Davis Islands Beach and Dog Beach
aliases: Davis Islands Dog Park & Dog Beach
places.hours_text: Sunrise to sunset.
places.summary: One of four City of Tampa beaches, at the Davis Islands Seaplane Basin; the city's fenced Davis Islands Dog Park and Dog Beach is next to it on Severn Avenue.
places.notes: Dog park and dog beach address: 1002 Severn St. (city dog-park page).

places.name: Al Lopez Park
places.hours_text: Sunrise to sunset.
places.summary: A 132-acre City of Tampa park with a paved loop trail around a lake, a boardwalk nature trail, a freshwater fishing dock, the fenced Jim Urbanski Dog Park, playgrounds and the Cordelia B. Hunt Community Center.
places.status_note: Open. The dog park is closed Thursdays from opening until noon for maintenance (city advisories page, Sep 2026).
places.notes: Area: the park is north of Raymond James Stadium on Himes Ave; west-tampa chosen as the nearest area in SPEC 4.1.

places.name: Water Works Park
places.hours_text: Daily, 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.
places.price_text: No admission fee.
places.summary: A free City of Tampa riverfront park on the Riverwalk near Armature Works, with a splash pad, a playground, Queenie's Dog Park, shaded picnic shelters, a festival lawn and a Pirate Water Taxi stop. It is a park, not a water park.
places.quote: Water Works Park is a City park (not a water park) open to the public. There is no admission fee.

places.name: Ballast Point Park
places.hours_text: Park 6 a.m. to 8 p.m.; splash pad 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.; boat ramp 24 hours.
places.summary: A City of Tampa park on Hillsborough Bay in South Tampa with views of downtown, a splash pad, a playground, picnic shelters, a gazebo, a boat ramp and Leons Lobstah Shack. Its 600-foot fishing pier has been closed since spring 2025 for hurricane repairs.
places.status_note: Park open; the 600-foot pier has been closed since spring 2025 after damage from Hurricanes Helene and Milton (city page, updated Feb 4, 2026). The page's intro also says the fitness center is closed, while its fitness-center section says it has reopened.

places.name: Lowry Park
places.hours_text: Sunrise to sunset.
places.summary: A City of Tampa park on the Hillsborough River across from ZooTampa, with the 0.9-mile paved Lowry Park Trail through oak hammocks along the river, fishing docks, a canoe and boat launch, picnic shelters and grills. HART routes 44 and 45 stop nearby.
places.notes: A search snippet gave 7525 N Boulevard; the city trail page says 7252 N Boulevard, which census matched. ZooTampa is a separate record (zootampa-at-lowry-park, see-tampa).

places.name: Tampa Electric's Manatee Viewing Center
places.hours_text: Open daily Nov. 1 to Apr. 15, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.; trails and observation tower close at 4 p.m. Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas Day and Easter; closes at 3 p.m. on Christmas Eve.
places.price_text: Free admission and parking.
places.summary: In winter, manatees gather in the warm, clean discharge canal of Tampa Electric's Big Bend Power Station, a state and federal manatee sanctuary; the free center has boardwalks and a 900-foot tidal walk to watch them, a cownose ray touch tank, an education building, a coastal habitat trail and a cafe.
places.quote: In the winter months the manatees leave colder waters to return to this warm and welcoming refuge.
places.status_note: Closed for the off-season; reopens Nov. 1, 2026 (Tampa Electric page, read Sep 27, 2026).
places.accessibility: The 900-foot tidal walk is ADA compliant.

places.name: Honeymoon Island State Park
places.hours_text: Daily, 8 a.m. until sundown. Rotary Centennial Nature Center: Wednesday to Sunday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
places.price_text: $8 per vehicle (up to eight people); $4 single-occupant vehicle; $2 pedestrians and bicyclists.
places.summary: A barrier-island state park in Dunedin with about four miles of Gulf beach, a leashed-pet beach, paved paths, a 2.5-mile nature trail through slash pine forest, a nature center, a cafe and bike, kayak and chair rentals. The ferry to Caladesi Island leaves from here.
places.quote: four miles of unspoiled white-sand beach lapped by clear, calm Gulf water
places.status_note: Open. Hurricanes Helene and Milton (2024) damaged the park; Visit St. Pete/Clearwater's beach-conditions page (read Sep 27, 2026) says all St. Pete-Clearwater beaches are open with no advisories.
places.notes: floridastateparks.org returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to both WebFetch and curl on 2026-09-27, so the park's own page could not be read; facts come from the pages cited. Visit Tampa Bay's listing says leashed dogs are welcome on the southeast side. Hurricane repair status of individual facilities (bathhouses) not confirmed.

places.name: Caladesi Island State Park
places.hours_text: Daily, 8 a.m. to sunset.
places.price_text: Ferry round trip from Honeymoon Island: adults $20, children 6-12 $10, 5 and under free (tickets sold only at the ferry office in Honeymoon Island State Park); Honeymoon Island park entry also applies.
places.summary: An undeveloped barrier island reached by a 20-minute ferry from Honeymoon Island or by private boat, with three miles of beach, a three-mile nature trail, a kayak trail through the mangroves, a marina, picnic pavilions and a concession. The ferry operator lists Dr. Beach rankings for it, most recently No. 3 in 2026.
places.quote: Caladesi Island State Park is a rare combination – a Florida Gulf Coast barrier island that is both remote and natural, and yet well stocked with amenities.
places.status_note: Open. The Caladesi Island Ferry's site (read Sep 27, 2026) shows daily departures and reviews from August 2026; it runs every day except Thanksgiving and Christmas, weather permitting.
places.accessibility: Beach wheelchairs are available on request from the ranger station, (727) 469-5918 (Caladesi Island Ferry page).
places.notes: floridastateparks.org returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to both WebFetch and curl on 2026-09-27, so the park's own page could not be read; facts come from the pages cited. Coordinates are the park GPS point printed on the ferry operator's Caladesi Island page. Wikipedia says the island can also be reached on foot from the north end of Clearwater Beach. 'No dogs on the ferry' is from a Google review quoted on the ferry homepage, not an official rule.

places.name: Egmont Key State Park
places.hours_text: Daily, 8 a.m. to sunset.
places.price_text: No park admission fee; ferry or boat fare applies.
places.summary: An island state park and national wildlife refuge at the mouth of Tampa Bay, reached only by boat, with the 1858 Egmont Key Lighthouse (tower closed to the public), the ruins of Fort Dade, brick roads, gopher tortoises and beaches for shelling and snorkeling. There is no drinking water, restroom or shop on the island, and pets are not allowed.
places.quote: Egmont Key is a pristine island, so there isn’t a bathroom or any type of shop on the island so make sure to come prepared with a cooler full of water, food and drinks.

designations.name: National Register of Historic Places (Egmont Key)

heritage.story: Egmont Key's lighthouse dates from 1858 and is maintained by the U.S. Coast Guard. Fort Dade was built in 1898 and served during the Spanish-American War; it never saw battle but was a military reservation guarding the entrance to Tampa Bay until 1923. The island became a national wildlife refuge in 1974 and is managed with the Florida Park Service. Hurricanes Helene and Milton in 2024 sent storm surge about 15 feet up the lighthouse, and the island was closed for more than six months.
heritage.visiting: Boat or ferry only. Visitors can walk the fort ruins, gun batteries and brick roads; the lighthouse tower is closed to the public.

places.status_note: Open. Hubbard's Marina runs the Egmont Key ferry from Fort De Soto daily at 9 and 11 a.m., plus 2 p.m. on Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday (ferry page, read Sep 27, 2026). The Egmont Key Alliance says the island was closed for 6+ months after the 2024 hurricanes; Visit St. Pete/Clearwater notes storm damage and overgrowth limit access to some historic sites.
places.notes: floridastateparks.org returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to both WebFetch and curl on 2026-09-27, so the park's own page could not be read; facts come from the pages cited. Egmont Key is in Hillsborough County; area set to fort-de-soto (SPEC 4.1 lists Egmont Key there). Acreage differs by source (Wikipedia 328 acres for the refuge; Visit St. Pete/Clearwater 440 acres), so none is stated. Wikipedia's ferry times (10 and 11 a.m.) are older than Hubbard's current page (9 and 11 a.m.).

places.name: Anclote Key Preserve State Park

heritage.story: George Turner Sr., a plumber and gardener, bought the land in 1911, drained the sinkhole called Curlew Pond with clay tiles and by the early 1930s charged fifteen cents for tours. His sons brought the first flamingos in 1955, and the family ran the gardens as a roadside attraction for three generations before putting them up for sale in 1989. St. Petersburg voters approved a one-time tax increase to save them; the gardens became a local historic landmark in 1998, and the main entrance was listed in the National Register in 1999.

places.summary: An 8,300-acre Pasco County wilderness park run with the Southwest Florida Water Management District, with a 7.3-mile paved trail that connects to the Suncoast Trail, a 10-mile equestrian trail, 13 miles of hiking trails, an Audubon-designated birding trail, and cabins, tent and primitive camping.
places.notes: Dogs on 6-foot leashes are allowed in the day-use area and on the hiking and paved trails, not in the camping area or on the equestrian trail. Coordinates are the county page's map link.

places.name: Robert K. Rees Memorial Park
places.hours_text: Daily, sunrise to sunset.
places.summary: A 45-acre Pasco County beach park with a beach and swim area, a boardwalk, an observation deck, kayak and canoe access, fishing, a playground and picnic shelters.
places.notes: Coordinates are the county page's map link.

places.name: Robert J. Strickland Memorial Park
places.hours_text: Daily, sunrise to sunset.
places.summary: A 6-acre Pasco County beach park in Hudson with a beach and swim area, a boardwalk, an observation tower, a dock, kayak and canoe access, picnic shelters and restaurants nearby; the boat ramp is at 14104 Armand Way.
places.notes: Coordinates are the county page's map link. 'Hudson Beach' alias is the common local name; verify.

places.name: Anclote Gulf Park
places.summary: A 23-acre Pasco County natural resource park with a fishing pier and a trail for watching birds, a boardwalk to Key Vista Park, canoe access, a dog park and a playground.
places.notes: Listed on the Pasco directory under Gulf Coast Parks. Coordinates are the county page's map link.

places.name: Alfred McKethan Pine Island Park
aliases: Alfred A. McKethan Park at Pine Island
places.hours_text: Daily, 8:30 a.m. to sunset.
places.price_text: $5 per car (credit card only).
places.summary: A 3-acre Hernando County park on the Gulf west of Weeki Wachee with a beach and swimming area, shelters, grills, a volleyball court, a playground, an observation point and a concession stand. No RVs, buses or trailers.
places.notes: The page gives both 10800 and 10840 Pine Island Drive; the address block uses 10840 (census match).

places.name: Rogers Park
places.hours_text: Open 24/7.
places.summary: A 3-acre Hernando County beach park on the Weeki Wachee River for swimming, canoeing, fishing and boat launching, with a canoe launch, showers, an observation deck, a playground and shelters. The county does not rent kayaks here, and no lifeguards are on duty.
places.quote: If fresh water is more your style, try this 3-acre beach park on the Weeki Wachee River, where you can swim, canoe, fish, launch a boat, or maybe even spot a manatee!
places.notes: The page lists seasonal lifeguards among amenities but also says no lifeguards are on duty; summary uses the notice. Point is the OSM 'Rogers Park Beach' feature.

places.name: Fort Island Gulf Beach
places.summary: Citrus County's 15-acre Gulf beach near Crystal River, with a fishing pier, a boat ramp and picnic tables. No lifeguards, no pets, and no fishing from the beach or jetties.
places.status_note: Open while renovations and repairs continue; portable restrooms on site (Citrus County page, read Sep 27, 2026).
places.notes: Coordinates are the fishing-pier lat/long printed on the county page.

places.name: Morris Bridge Conservation Park
places.hours_text: Fall and winter 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.; spring and summer 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.
places.price_text: $2 per vehicle, up to 8 people.
places.summary: A Hillsborough County park on the Hillsborough River where alligators, turtles and wading birds are often seen, with a boardwalk, hiking trails and a canoe launch; the Wilderness Trail links off-road cyclists to Flatwoods and Trout Creek parks.
places.quote: Wildlife abounds at this park along the Hillsborough River, with frequent sightings of alligators, turtles, water snakes, frogs, and wading birds.
places.status_note: Partly closed: the boat ramp and the park's west side are closed while the state clears damage along the Hillsborough River, and all public river access from John B. Sargeant Park to Trout Creek Park is closed until further notice (county notice, page updated Aug 20, 2026).

places.name: Clam Bayou Nature Preserve
places.summary: A City of St. Petersburg preserve used by kayakers and paddlers, with recreation trails and a link to the county Blueways paddling trail system.
places.quote: Clam Bayou Nature Preserve is a great destination for avid kayakers or paddlers and nature enthusiast.
places.notes: Thin source (the city's preserves list). Area set to gulfport because the preserve sits on the St. Petersburg-Gulfport line (coordinates).

places.name: Chassahowitzka National Wildlife Refuge
places.address: 6112 S. Mason Creek Road (Salt Marsh Trails)
places.hours_text: Sunrise to sunset, year round.
places.summary: About 31,000 acres of saltwater bays, estuaries and brackish marsh roughly 65 miles north of St. Petersburg, reached mostly by boat from the Citrus County ramp at the end of State Road 480 for paddling the clear Chassahowitzka River; on land, the Salt Marsh Trails off Mason Creek Road lead to the Lastinger observation tower.
places.notes: Point is the Salt Marsh Trails parking address given by USFWS. 76 percent of the refuge is designated wilderness.

stays.name: Fort De Soto Park Campground
stays.summary: A 236-site county campground inside Fort De Soto Park; every site has water and 30/50-amp electric, a picnic table and a grill, with restrooms, showers, laundry, dump stations and a camp store. Pets are allowed in sites 86-164 only. Nightly base rates run $40.50 to $47.50 plus tax, and non-residents can book six months ahead.
stays.quote: This 236-site family camping area includes convenient facilities such as picnic tables, grills, water, electricity, washers, dryers, sanitary disposal stations, modern restrooms, showers, play areas and a campground store.
stays.notes: Coordinates are the park centroid, not the campground. Camp office 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily; check-in after 1 p.m., checkout 11 a.m.; max 14 nights in 30 days; gate locked 9 p.m. to 5:30 a.m.

stays.name: E.G. Simmons Conservation Park Campground
stays.summary: A 110-site Hillsborough County campground on Tampa Bay inside E.G. Simmons Conservation Park; sites have electricity, water, picnic tables and fire pits, with shower houses and two RV dump stations. The regular rate is $24 a night for up to 8 people.
stays.notes: 2 primitive sites without electricity; all sites 30-amp, 62 also 50-amp; sites 35 to 160 feet. Discounts: $18 (55+), $12 (65+ county residents).

stays.name: Lithia Springs Conservation Park Campground
stays.summary: A 45-site Hillsborough County campground at Lithia Springs, most sites suitable for RVs, with water, electricity, restrooms with showers and fire pits; the regular rate is $24 a night for up to 8 people.
stays.notes: Two of the 45 sites are host sites; all 30-amp, 15 also 50-amp.

stays.name: Edward Medard Conservation Park Campground
stays.summary: A 43-site Hillsborough County campground for RVs and tents at the Medard Reservoir; every site has a picnic table, electricity, a fire ring and water, with restrooms, showers and an RV dump station. The regular rate is $24 a night for up to 8 people.

stays.name: Alderman's Ford Conservation Park Primitive Campsites
stays.summary: Four hike-in primitive campsites, about a 1 to 1.5 mile walk from parking, with picnic tables, hammock stands and fire pits but no water or electricity; reserve by calling the park office.

stays.name: Terry Tomalin Campground

# outdoors slice: report (read Sep 27, 2026)

## What is covered
90 places and 12 campground/cabin records (stays, kind campground).

Places by kind: 26 beaches, 24 parks, 14 nature preserves, 13 state parks, 6 gardens, 6 trails, 1 pier.
Places by region: Day Trips 23, Gulf Beaches 16, Tampa 16, Around the Bay 15, Clearwater & North Pinellas 13, St. Petersburg 7.
Stays by region: Around the Bay 8, Day Trips 2, Gulf Beaches 1 (Fort De Soto), St. Petersburg 1 (Terry Tomalin).

- **Gulf beaches, Pinellas:** Fort De Soto (shared id), Shell Key, Egmont Key, Pass-a-Grille, St. Pete Beach Access, Treasure Island Beach, Sunset Beach, St. Petersburg Municipal Beach at Treasure Island, Madeira Beach Access, Archibald, John's Pass Beach, Redington Shores Access, Tiki Gardens/Indian Shores Access, Indian Rocks Beach Access, Sand Key Park, Clearwater public beach, Caladesi, Honeymoon, Fred Howard, Anclote Key.
- **Bay beaches:** Ben T. Davis, Cypress Point, Picnic Island, Davis Islands (with the dog beach), North Shore Park, Apollo Beach Nature Preserve, E.G. Simmons, Anna Maria Bayfront Park.
- **Day-trip beaches:** Manatee Public Beach, Coquina Beach, Siesta Beach, Lido Beach; Nature Coast: Pine Island, Rogers Park (river beach), Fort Island Gulf Beach; Pasco: Robert K. Rees and Robert J. Strickland parks.
- **Dog beaches** (tag `dog-beach`): Fort De Soto, Honeymoon Island, Picnic Island, Davis Islands.
- **State parks:** Honeymoon, Caladesi, Egmont Key, Anclote Key, Skyway Fishing Pier, Hillsborough River, Alafia River, Little Manatee River, Weeki Wachee (shared id), Ellie Schiller Homosassa Springs Wildlife, Crystal River Preserve, Myakka River, Oscar Scherer, Lake Manatee. USFWS: Three Sisters Springs, Crystal River NWR, Chassahowitzka NWR.
- **County and city parks and preserves:** Pinellas (Weedon Island, Sawgrass Lake, Brooker Creek, Philippe with the Safety Harbor mound as a heritage block, Lake Seminole, John Chesnut Sr., Wall Springs, Boca Ciega Millennium); St. Petersburg (Boyd Hill, Clam Bayou); Clearwater (Moccasin Lake); Hillsborough (Lettuce Lake, Upper Tampa Bay, Lithia Springs, Edward Medard, Alderman's Ford, Flatwoods, Morris Bridge, Eureka Springs); Tampa (Lowry Park, Al Lopez, Water Works, Ballast Point); Manatee (Robinson, Emerson Point); Polk (Circle B Bar); Pasco (Starkey, Anclote Gulf Park).
- **Gardens:** Florida Botanical Gardens, Sunken Gardens (shared id, heritage block), USF Botanical Gardens, Eureka Springs, Marie Selby, Bok Tower Gardens (heritage block).
- **Trails:** Pinellas Trail, Upper Tampa Bay Trail, Selmon Greenway, Courtney Campbell Causeway Trail, Suncoast Trail, Withlacoochee State Trail. Four linear trails have no single point and no coordinates.
- **Wildlife and springs:** TECO Manatee Viewing Center (status `seasonal`: reopens Nov. 1, 2026), Three Sisters Springs, Crystal River NWR, Homosassa, Weeki Wachee, Lithia Springs, Wall Springs.
- **Campgrounds and cabins:** Fort De Soto; Hillsborough County's E.G. Simmons, Lithia Springs, Edward Medard and Alderman's Ford primitive sites; St. Petersburg's Terry Tomalin (18 sites, 6 cabins); Starkey (cabins, tent, primitive); state parks: Hillsborough River, Alafia River, Little Manatee River, Myakka River (with palm-log cabins), Lake Manatee. The state-park campground records are thin (see below).

## How candidates were found
1. Official lists: Pinellas County's parks index and beach-access list (pinellas.gov/parks, /beaches, park updates page), Hillsborough County location pages (hcfl.gov), City of Tampa featured parks, beaches, dog parks, advisories and greenways pages, St. Petersburg Parks & Recreation (beaches, preserves, Boyd Hill), Manatee County's boat-ramps-and-beaches list, the Pasco park directory, Hernando County's parks list, Citrus County's parks and beaches pages.
2. Visit Tampa Bay's listings API (Simpleview find endpoint for the outdoors, beaches and campground subcategories, plus a title search for park/preserve/beach/garden/trail/spring/island), and Visit St. Pete/Clearwater's beaches, outdoors, nature-preserve and beach-conditions pages (read with WebFetch).
3. Wikipedia articles for the state parks, trails and Sarasota beaches; USFWS refuge pages.
4. The session's WebSearch budget ran out early (200/200), so later discovery used site navigation and the lists above.

## Status (Helene and Milton) findings
- Pinellas County park updates (Sep 25, 2026): Fort De Soto Bay Pier far end closed for hurricane repairs, boat-ramp docks replaced in phases, road/trail repaving; Weedon Island Bay Boardwalk section closed to late 2026; Sand Key seawall section closed to October 2026; playground and restroom work at Philippe, Wall Springs and others. County beach parking becomes $3.50/hour (cap $12/day) on Dec. 1, 2026.
- Clearwater: Pier 60 open only to the fishing pier; bait house and fishing pier closed (Pier 60 itself belongs to see-pinellas).
- St. Petersburg Municipal Beach at Treasure Island: beach and lot open, building and amenities closed.
- Tampa: Ballast Point pier closed since spring 2025. Hillsborough County: Lettuce Lake boardwalk sections, tower and kayak launch closed; Morris Bridge boat ramp and all river access from John B. Sargeant to Trout Creek closed; Medard boat ramp closed (reservoir drawdown).
- Manatee County: Robinson Preserve tram tours cancelled after hurricane damage; Emerson Point dock closed. Citrus: Fort Island Gulf Beach open with repairs.
- Egmont Key was closed 6+ months after the 2024 storms (Egmont Key Alliance); the Hubbard's ferry now runs daily. Hillsborough River State Park closed Oct 2024 and reopened Feb 24, 2025 (Wikipedia).
- Visit St. Pete/Clearwater's beach-conditions page: "All St. Pete-Clearwater beaches are open, with no advisories."

## Left out, and why
- floridastateparks.org (and the Guest Services concession sites weekiwachee.com, homosassaspringswildlife.com, crystalriverpreserveadventures.com) returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to both WebFetch and curl. State-park records therefore rest on Wikipedia, Visit Tampa Bay / Visit St. Pete-Clearwater listings, ferry operators and county pages. Hours and fees are null for most state parks, and their `url` fields follow the site's URL pattern without having been opened.
- Sarasota County (scgov.net), Visit Sarasota listing pages, City of Crystal River, Three Sisters Springs Center, Dunedin, Gulfport, Tarpon Springs city and Polk County park pages were blocked or script-rendered. Turtle Beach, Crescent Beach, Nokomis/Venice beaches, Hunter Springs Park, Hammock Park and the Dunedin Causeway, Gulfport Beach, Sunset Beach (Tarpon Springs), Largo Central Park Nature Preserve and the Legacy Trail were therefore not added.
- Gandy Beach (bay beach on the Gandy Blvd causeway, named in the brief): no official or tourism page describing it was found (the Pinellas County and St. Petersburg sites have none). Beer Can Island / Pine Key: privately owned; no official page found. Both left out.
- Skipped as low visitor interest: Walsingham, Eagle Lake, A.L. Anderson and Taylor parks (Pinellas), Werner-Boyce Salt Springs (Wikipedia outdated, official page blocked), Terra Ceia, Fort Cooper, Wolf Branch Creek, Palma Sola Causeway Park (no usable geocode), Spa Beach (part of the St. Pete Pier), Lassing and Maximo parks.
- Left to other slices: Crystal River Archaeological State Park, Historic Spanish Point, De Soto National Memorial, Madira Bickel Mound (history-region); the Tampa Riverwalk and Bayshore Boulevard (see-tampa); Pier 60 and the St. Pete Pier (see-pinellas); ferries and kayak/manatee tours (exp-water).

## Open questions for the verifier
1. State parks: confirm current status, hours and fees on floridastateparks.org from a browser, especially Weeki Wachee (Helene flooding), Honeymoon (bathhouses), Caladesi, Little Manatee, Alafia, Myakka, Lake Manatee, Anclote Key, Oscar Scherer and the Skyway Pier. Also confirm the `url` slugs for Anclote Key, Skyway Pier, Little Manatee, Lake Manatee, Oscar Scherer, Myakka and the Withlacoochee trail.
2. The state-park campground stays (Hillsborough River, Little Manatee, Alafia, Myakka, Lake Manatee) are thin, based on Wikipedia and one listing; drop or enrich them.
3. Weeki Wachee NRHP year: Wikipedia's infobox says 2009 (ref 09000843), its text says 2020; no year was recorded.
4. Florida Botanical Gardens hours conflict: the gardens page says 7 a.m. to 5 p.m.; the county hours page says 7 a.m. to sunset.
5. Archibald Memorial Beach Park: the official name and details rest on a Visit Tampa Bay listing only.
6. Point accuracy: USF Botanical Gardens (street match), Flatwoods (road inside the park), Hillsborough River, Myakka, Lake Manatee and Little Manatee (park centroids), Clearwater Beach (OSM place node).
